verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.34
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 3.34

verses.pali: 4. Devadūtavagga
verses.english: 4. Messengers of the Gods

verses.pali: Nidānasutta
verses.english: Sources

verses.pali: “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāya.
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these three sources that give rise to deeds.

verses.pali: Katamāni tīṇi?
verses.english: What three?

verses.pali: Lobho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, doso nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, moho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya.
verses.english: Greed, hate, and delusion are sources that give rise to deeds.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, lobhapakataṁ kammaṁ lobhajaṁ lobhanidānaṁ lobhasamudayaṁ, yatthassa attabhāvo nibbattati tattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati.
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from greed—born, sourced, and originated from greed—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

verses.pali: Yattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati tattha tassa kammassa vipākaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, diṭṭhe vā dhamme upapajja vā apare vā pariyāye.
verses.english: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, dosapakataṁ kammaṁ dosajaṁ dosanidānaṁ dosasamudayaṁ, yatthassa attabhāvo nibbattati tattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati.
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from hate—born, sourced, and originated from hate—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

verses.pali: Yattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati tattha tassa kammassa vipākaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, diṭṭhe vā dhamme upapajja vā apare vā pariyāye.
verses.english: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, mohapakataṁ kammaṁ mohajaṁ mohanidānaṁ mohasamudayaṁ, yatthassa attabhāvo nibbattati tattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati.
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from delusion—born, sourced, and originated from delusion—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

verses.pali: Yattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati tattha tassa kammassa vipākaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, diṭṭhe vā dhamme upapajja vā apare vā pariyāye.
verses.english: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, bījāni akhaṇḍāni apūtīni avātātapahatāni sārādāni sukhasayitāni sukhette suparikammakatāya bhūmiyā nikkhittāni.
verses.english: Suppose some seeds were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. They’re sown in a well-prepared, productive field,

verses.pali: Devo ca sammādhāraṁ anuppaveccheyya.
verses.english: and the heavens provide plenty of rain.

verses.pali: Evassu tāni, bhikkhave, bījāni vuddhiṁ viruḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyyuṁ.
verses.english: Then those seeds would grow, increase, and mature.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yaṁ lobhapakataṁ kammaṁ lobhajaṁ lobhanidānaṁ lobhasamudayaṁ, yatthassa attabhāvo nibbattati tattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati.
verses.english: In the same way, any deed that emerges from greed—born, sourced, and originated from greed—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

verses.pali: Yattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati tattha tassa kammassa vipākaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, diṭṭhe vā dhamme upapajja vā apare vā pariyāye.
verses.english: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

verses.pali: Yaṁ dosapakataṁ kammaṁ …pe…
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from hate …

verses.pali: yaṁ mohapakataṁ kammaṁ mohajaṁ mohanidānaṁ mohasamudayaṁ, yatthassa attabhāvo nibbattati tattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati.
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from delusion—born, sourced, and originated from delusion—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

verses.pali: Yattha taṁ kammaṁ vipaccati tattha tassa kammassa vipākaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, diṭṭhe vā dhamme upapajja vā apare vā pariyāye.
verses.english: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

verses.pali: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāya.
verses.english: These are three sources that give rise to deeds.

verses.pali: Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāya.
verses.english: Mendicants, there are these three sources that give rise to deeds.

verses.pali: Katamāni tīṇi?
verses.english: What three?

verses.pali: Alobho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, adoso nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya, amoho nidānaṁ kammānaṁ samudayāya.
verses.english: Contentment, love, and understanding are sources that give rise to deeds.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, alobhapakataṁ kammaṁ alobhajaṁ alobhanidānaṁ alobhasamudayaṁ, lobhe vigate evaṁ taṁ kammaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from contentment—born, sourced, and originated from contentment—is given up when greed is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, adosapakataṁ kammaṁ adosajaṁ adosanidānaṁ adosasamudayaṁ, dose vigate evaṁ taṁ kammaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from love—born, sourced, and originated from love—is abandoned when hate is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

verses.pali: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, amohapakataṁ kammaṁ amohajaṁ amohanidānaṁ amohasamudayaṁ, mohe vigate evaṁ taṁ kammaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from understanding—born, sourced, and originated from understanding—is abandoned when delusion is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, bījāni akhaṇḍāni apūtīni avātātapahatāni sārādāni sukhasayitāni.
verses.english: Suppose some seeds were intact, unspoiled, not damaged by wind and sun, fertile, and well-kept.

verses.pali: Tāni puriso agginā ḍaheyya.
verses.english: But someone would burn them with fire,

verses.pali: Agginā ḍahitvā masiṁ kareyya.
verses.english: reduce them to ashes,

verses.pali: Masiṁ karitvā mahāvāte vā ophuṇeyya nadiyā vā sīghasotāya pavāheyya.
verses.english: and whisk away the ashes in a strong wind, or glide them down a swift stream.

verses.pali: Evassu tāni, bhikkhave, bījāni ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṁ anuppādadhammāni.
verses.english: Then those seeds would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yaṁ alobhapakataṁ kammaṁ alobhajaṁ alobhanidānaṁ alobhasamudayaṁ, lobhe vigate evaṁ taṁ kammaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
verses.english: In the same way, any deed that emerges from contentment—born, sourced, and originated from contentment—is abandoned when greed is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

verses.pali: Yaṁ adosapakataṁ kammaṁ …pe…
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from love …

verses.pali: yaṁ amohapakataṁ kammaṁ amohajaṁ amohanidānaṁ amohasamudayaṁ, mohe vigate evaṁ taṁ kammaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti …pe…
verses.english: Any deed that emerges from understanding—born, sourced, and originated from understanding—is abandoned when delusion is done away with.

verses.pali: āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
verses.english: It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

verses.pali: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi nidānāni kammānaṁ samudayāyāti.
verses.english: These are three sources that give rise to deeds.

verses.pali: Lobhajaṁ dosajañceva,
verses.english: When an ignorant person acts

verses.pali: mohajañcāpaviddasu;
verses.english: out of greed, hate, or delusion,

verses.pali: Yaṁ tena pakataṁ kammaṁ,
verses.english: any deeds they have done,

verses.pali: appaṁ vā yadi vā bahuṁ;
verses.english: a little or a lot,

verses.pali: Idheva taṁ vedaniyaṁ,
verses.english: are to be experienced right here,

verses.pali: vatthu aññaṁ na vijjati.
verses.english: not in any other place.

verses.pali: Tasmā lobhañca dosañca,
verses.english: So a wise person,

verses.pali: mohajañcāpi viddasu;
verses.english: a mendicant arousing knowledge

verses.pali: Vijjaṁ uppādayaṁ bhikkhu,
verses.english: of the outcome of greed, hate, and delusion,

verses.pali: sabbā duggatiyo jahe”ti.
verses.english: would abandon all bad destinies.”

verses.pali: Catutthaṁ.
